# Mac App Store apps

Jamf **Mac App Store Apps** objects live on Classic `/JSSResource/macapplications`. There is no Pro JSON catalog CRUD for the same resource. Classic privileges on an instance-surface auth are required.

Bare `buddy app` / `apps(...)` manage **policy apps** (Self Service + packages) — see [Policy apps](/docs/docs/apps). Those names are a different resource family from Mac App Store records.

## Agent rules

- Do not invent Pro “Mac App Store” or “Jamf Apps” list/create paths — they are not exposed for this object.
- Do not confuse this with VPP locations/content (`/api/v1/volume-purchasing-locations`) or `jamf-package` (Protect/Connect only).
- Do not use `app` / `apps` for MAS records — those builtins are policy apps; see [Policy apps](/docs/docs/apps).
- Prefer an instance-surface auth (Classic privileges).

## Facts

- List: `macapps(filter?)` · `buddy macapp list` — Client-side substring; Classic list has no RSQL
- Load: `macapp(id=…)` / `macapp(name=…)` · `buddy macapp get` — Full Classic record
- Create: `macapp_create(...)` · `buddy macapp create` — Requires name, version, bundle_id, url
- Delete: `macapp_delete(id)` · `buddy macapp delete`
- Classic `/JSSResource/macapplications` only — no Pro JSON catalog CRUD. Instance-surface auth with Classic privileges is required.

## Examples

```python
def main():
    rows = macapps(filter="TextWrangler")
    if not rows:
        return macapp_create(
            name="TextWrangler.app",
            version="5.5.2",
            bundle_id="com.barebones.textwrangler",
            url="https://itunes.apple.com/app/id404010395",
            free=True,
        )
    return macapp(id=rows[0]["id"])
```
